passage:
Gargi, come sit. Your Neelam Masi was twenty once too, and I want to tell you about Rohan.

He brought me tea at the library every evening. He remembered my exam dates before I did. Nobody had ever fussed over me like that, and I'd glow for an hour and then get a knot in my stomach. What if I couldn't be that person for him?

So one night I said it aloud: "I like you very much, but I'm not ready to promise big things." He went quiet, then nodded, and stayed anyway.

And I kept my Thursday evenings with Shanti and the hostel girls. Once I forgot to thank him for the tea and noticed only when he stopped bringing it for two days. I thanked him properly after that.

qa.q: What did Rohan do at the library every evening?
qa.a: Rohan brought Neelam tea at the library every evening.

qa.q: Why did being chosen feel both warm and frightening to Neelam?
qa.a: It felt warm to be valued so much, but she worried she could not live up to that devotion, which is why she spoke honestly about not being ready.

qa.q: What would you tell someone who has just been chosen with this kind of devotion?
qa.a: Be honest about what you can and cannot promise, keep your own friendships going, and say thank you instead of taking the care for granted.

qa.q: How might Rohan have felt when Neelam said she was not ready to promise big things?
qa.a: He may have been disappointed for a moment, but also relieved to know where she stood instead of guessing.

grounding: Shows the warmth and slight fear of being chosen, met with honesty about limits and keeping one's own friendships.

passage: Student counselling note, Monday. Suraj (third year, commerce) came in to talk about his relationship with Tanvir, now six months long. He described Tanvir planning surprise dinners, remembering every exam date, and recently saying he sees a future with him. Suraj said it feels warm and also frightening: he has never felt that chosen before and worries he can't match it. He admitted he had skipped two football evenings with his friends to be available, and felt quietly resentful. We talked about receiving care honestly: thanking Tanvir, saying clearly what he can and can't give right now, and keeping his own friendships rather than disappearing into the relationship. Suraj decided to tell Tanvir this week, 'I love how you show up for me. I'm slower with big words, and I need my Thursday football.' He left looking lighter. Follow-up in two weeks.

qa.q: What has Suraj skipped to be available for Tanvir?
qa.a: Two football evenings with his friends.

qa.q: How does Suraj feel about being so chosen by Tanvir?
qa.a: He feels warm and also frightened, worried he can't match Tanvir's devotion.

qa.q: What did Suraj plan to tell Tanvir, and why is it healthy?
qa.a: That he loves how Tanvir shows up but is slower with big words and needs his Thursday football, being honest about limits and keeping friendships.

qa.q: How might Tanvir feel hearing Suraj's words?
qa.a: Possibly a little unsure at first, but reassured by the honesty and the thanks.

grounding: A counsellor's note on a young man who feels chosen by his partner, receiving it with honesty about his limits and keeping his friendships.

passage:
Tuesday night. Rashmi surprised me today with a whole notebook of things she'd noticed about me over the year: the way I hum when I'm nervous, how I always give the last samosa away. I cried in the library. Nobody has ever paid that much attention to me. And then, on the walk back, a small scary feeling: what if I can't give her this much back? What if she expects me every evening now? I noticed I'd already said no to Meera's birthday dinner on Friday because Rashmi had 'maybe' plans. That's not fair to Meera, or to me. So tonight I called Rashmi and said it honestly: 'I love this. I love you. I'm also someone who needs my friends and quiet evenings, and I'm not great at grand gestures.' She laughed and said she knew, and that's partly why she likes me. I'm going to Meera's dinner. I wrote Rashmi a small thank-you note back.
- Aadhya

qa.a: A notebook of things she'd noticed over the year.

qa.q: What did Aadhya feel on the walk back from the library?
qa.a: Aadhya felt warm and loved, but also a small fear of not being able to give as much back.

qa.q: What did Aadhya do to receive the love honestly?
qa.a: Told Rashmi about needing friends and quiet evenings, kept Meera's dinner plan, and wrote a small thank-you note.

qa.q: How does Rashmi react to Aadhya's honesty?
qa.a: She laughs and says she already knew, and that it's part of why she likes Aadhya 🙂

grounding: A diary of a young person who feels deeply chosen, receiving it with honesty about their limits and keeping their own friendships.
